title: Motivational factors of digital self-harm among young adults in Germany
summary:
The study examines the forms of digital self-harm observed among young adults in Germany. It also aims to investigate the motivations behind the reported behaviors and whether these show similarities to findings regarding the motivations behind offline self-harm. The goal is to generate insights into digital self-harm in German-speaking countries that could be used in the future to develop interventions and intervention programs.

Background of the study:
Sometimes people intentionally harm themselves. This is called self-harming behavior. It is important to note that in most cases, self-harming behavior does not mean that the individuals involved want to die. Research has shown that the motivations behind self-harming behavior can be categorized into four overarching categories. More and more aspects of life are now taking place online. Consequently, self-harming behavior is also becoming more common in that context. Some people share or search for images or texts about how to harm themselves. The internet is also used to insult oneself or portray oneself in a negative light. This is called digital self-harm. In this case, the body is not injured, but emotional distress is inflicted. 

What is being done?
In a 20–25-minute, anonymous online survey, participants are asked about personal characteristics, current psychological distress, and various behaviors associated with digital and offline self-harm. They are asked to indicate the frequency of each behavior throughout their lives. If at least one behavior was reported, the survey then asks about the relevance of different motivations for the reported behavior. Finally, participants are asked how they learned about the survey. This is the last question. Afterward, they can enter a voluntary raffle. To do so, they must provide an email address. 

Who can participate?
Young adults aged 18 to 25 who currently reside in Germany are eligible to participate. Participants must also confirm that they feel mentally stable and capable of addressing the potentially distressing questions about self-harming behavior in the survey.

Aim of the study:
There is currently no reliable evidence on whether young people in Germany are affected by digital self-harm or why young adults engage in this behavior.  This makes it difficult to know whether programs to support those affected need to be developed. It is also difficult to plan what these programs might look like if we do not know why those affected engage in this behavior. Generating relevant data and integrating it into existing knowledge on online and offline self-harm are therefore the main objectives of this study.
Some of the questions may be uncomfortable for people experiencing mental distress. Therefore, we ask about their current state of mind and use this to determine at which point the survey is paused or terminated. If we did not take this into account, we could overlook important information and misjudge the situation. 

The main assumptions of the study are:
1. Various forms of digital self-harm also occur among young adults in Germany.
2. The motivations behind digital self-harm are the same as those behind offline self-harm.
3. Different motivations are particularly relevant for different forms of digital self-harm.
4. The findings regarding the motivations behind offline self-harm remain consistent even when the questionnaire is expanded to include items specific to digital self-harm.
5. People who are currently experiencing psychological distress are more likely to discontinue the survey than those who are not.
conditions: Digital self-harm, specifically the behaviors of self-cyberbullying and interaction with self-harm content related online, will be examined. In addition, non-suicidal self-injury (DSM-5 under “Conditions for Further Study”) will be assessed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Has mainly had their center of life in Germany, self-assessment as mentally stable enough to be able to deal with the issue of self-harming behavior
Exclusion criteria:
Has not had their center of life mainly in Germany, self-assessment as not mentally stable enough to be able to deal with the issue of self-harming behavior
